target_customer: Construction firms responsible for worker health and safety compliance on site
problem: Construction workers face noise, airborne particulate and UV exposure, and firms rely on periodic manual measurements or expensive wearables to manage and document it.
business_model: Hardware device plus cloud dashboard subscription (pilot stage, pricing not public)
product_category: Construction health and safety IoT sensors

founders.name: James Batstone
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page. TechCrunch (Aug 2016) says he and Michael Andrea worked together as product designers and smart cities researchers on a Royal College of Art project. Education and employers not otherwise stated.

founders.name: Michael Andrea
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch (Aug 2016), not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Off-the-shelf microphone, laser particle counter and UV sensors in a rugged hub with cloud dashboards (TechCrunch Aug 2016); standard hardware integration for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Built from off-the-shelf sensors per TechCrunch, so the hardware was copyable; no stated data or regulatory moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch described alternatives as inspector spot measurements and costly wearables; no incumbent response found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Aug 2016) says construction health risks such as noise, dust and UV are hard to monitor and firms must comply with regulation; pilots were running with unnamed construction firms.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself; another unrelated construction software product also used the name SmartSite.

outcome_analysis: SmartSite was a two person London hardware startup that got press in August 2016 during YC Summer 2016 and ran unnamed pilots. The YC directory lists it as inactive with no date or reason, and no shutdown post-mortem or news was found, so the cause is not public. Failure factors are left empty for that reason.
notes: Company site smartsitesafety.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch (treated as dead or down). Seed amount and dates rest on a single database (CB Insights, which also lists a total of 140K over 2 rounds); the Aug 22 2016 date matches the TechCrunch article date and may be a database artifact. Cofounders declined to disclose total raised. CB Insights lists the company as alive while YC lists it inactive. Competitor list is empty: TechCrunch names only generic alternatives and no dated named rival was found. No funding or outcome beyond this found.
